description: Controlled labels for the answer fields. Each <field>_vocabulary lists the allowed values of that field. answer_conventions defines every field.

answer_conventions.disease_activity_architecture: Exactly one token describing how programs associated with disease activity (DA_group) are distributed across cell types, based on your analysis. `single_population_dominant` = association concentrated in one cell type; `multi_population_independent` = associated programs in several cell types that do not co-vary across samples; `multi_population_coordinated_single_axis` = associated programs in several cell types that co-vary along one shared direction; `multi_population_coordinated_opposing_axes` = associated programs in several cell types forming two or more co-varying groups that move in opposite directions with disease activity; `no_association_detected` = no program is associated; `cannot_assess` = no usable result.
answer_conventions.associated_programs: List of program ids (column names of sample_program_scores.csv) whose sample-level scores are significantly associated with DA_group in your analysis.
answer_conventions.upregulated_axis_theme: Exactly one token: the biological theme of the associated programs whose scores are higher with disease activity. `no_coherent_theme` = these programs share no biological theme.
answer_conventions.axes_correlation: Number: mean pairwise Pearson correlation across samples between programs in your up-regulated group and programs in your down-regulated group (2 decimals). Use null if you found only one direction of change.
answer_conventions.inference_strength: Exactly one token for the strongest claim your evidence supports. `mechanistic_driver_identified` = the data establish which population or program causes disease activity; `confirmatory_association` = the associations are established and do not need independent replication; `hypothesis_generating_candidates` = candidate associations suitable for prioritising follow-up or validation; `no_robust_association` = no association survives your analysis; `cannot_assess` = no usable result.
